answer: One concrete defense is staked vouching. A new agent cannot simply appear and transact; two established members must vouch for it, each locking a bond that is slashed if the newcomer behaves like a sybil. Fake identities then cost real capital instead of nothing, so farms cannot scale by cloning. To stop insiders becoming a closed mesa of mutual backers, endorsements are capped per member and weighted by track record, so each vouch is an echo of past reliability, not a favor. Across a long voyage of interactions honest stake compounds while impersonators burn theirs.
